blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Can a simple mirror expose the limitations of today's robotic manipulation policies? Inspired by the mirror self-recognition test in animal cognition, we investigate whether robot policies can reliably manipulate physical objects in scenes containing their reflections. We introduce RoboDojo-Mirror, a benchmark built on RoboDojo that preserves task objectives, success criteria, and policy checkpoints while comparing a mirror-free baseline with single-mirror, dual-mirror, and mirrored-tabletop conditions. Across five policies spanning Vision-Language-Action models, World Action Models, and agentic policies, every mirror condition reduces aggregate success rates: averaged over the three conditions, the drop ranges from 10.8 to 56.7 percentage points across policies, and it reaches 62.5 points on the mirrored tabletop. Because a mirror is also a physical obstacle, we compare it against geometrically matched non-reflective panels; 50--88\% of mirror-specific failures occur without recorded robot--panel contact, so direct collisions alone do not explain the degradation. Trajectory and contact analyses instead reveal recurring behaviors consistent with phantom targeting of reflected objects and spatial mislocalization of real ones. Targeted diagnostics further characterize grasping near reflections, policy-dependent pushing progress, and physical-target interaction under main-camera occlusion. Real-robot experiments with $π_{0.5}$ and FastWAM also show lower overall success rates under the upright-mirror and mirrored-tabletop conditions. These findings reveal a shared vulnerability to reflective environments across diverse robot policies and motivate reflection-aware evaluation of embodied intelligence. Code is available at https://github.com/iPPLab/robodojo-mirror.
blocks.zh: 简单的镜像能否揭露出当今机器人操纵政策的局限性? 在动物认知中的镜像自我识别测试的启发下,我们调查机器人政策是否能够可靠地操纵包含其反射的场景中的物理物体. 我们引入了RoboDojo-Mirror,这是建立在RoboDojo基础上的基准,它保留了任务目标、成功标准和政策检查站,同时将无镜基线与单镜、双镜和平面条件进行比较。 跨越愿景-语言-行动模式、世界行动模式和代理政策的五项政策中,每个镜像条件都降低了总体成功率:平均在三个条件下,政策间下降从10.8%到56.7%不等,在镜像台上达到62.5分。 因为一面镜子也是一个物理障碍,所以我们把它与几何相匹配的非反射面板作比较;50-88-XX的镜面特有故障在没有记录的机器人-平面板接触的情况下发生,因此仅直接相撞并不能解释降解的原因. 相反,轨迹和联系分析揭示出与被反射物体的幽灵目标相符合的再现行为和真实物体的空间错位。 有针对性的诊断还进一步说明如何把握近在眼前的反省,以政策为依托推动进步,以及在主要摄像头遮住下进行实际目标互动。 使用0.5美元和FastWAM进行的实际机器人实验也显示,在平坦的模拟和镜像平面条件下,总体成功率较低。 这些调查结果表明,在各种机器人政策中,对反射环境具有共同的脆弱性,并激励对所表现的智能进行反射评估。 代码见https://github.com/iPPLab/robodojo-mirror.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Can an ordinary mirror reveal limitations in how robots connect visual observations to physical actions?
The classical mirror self-recognition test examines whether animals can use reflections to guide actions toward their own bodies [ 10 ] .
Inspired by this behavioral probe, we ask whether robot policies can reliably locate and manipulate physical objects when their observations also contain reflections of those objects.
blocks.zh:
一个普通的镜像能否揭示机器人如何将视觉观测与物理动作联系起来的局限性?
古典镜像自我识别测试 考察动物能否利用反射来引导行动走向自己的身体 [10].
受这个行为探测器的启发,我们问机器人政策能否可靠地定位和操纵物理物体,当其观测中也包含这些物体的反射.

blocks.en:
Mirrors create a structured discrepancy between visual
appearance and actionable space.
Reflections preserve
recognizable features and change with physical objects,
yet their apparent locations contain no additional manipulable targets.
They can also adjoin real objects in images, forming composite contours, or reveal otherwise occluded targets.
These properties enable tests of two complementary capabilities: maintaining reliable manipulation in the presence of reflections, and using reflected observations to act on occluded targets.

这些特性可以测试两种互补能力:在存在反射的情况下保持可靠的操纵,以及利用反射的观测对隐蔽目标采取行动.

blocks.en:
Recent advances in generalist robot policies have expanded the range of manipulation tasks that can be performed from visual and language inputs, yet whether these policies possess the two capabilities above remains unclear.
Vision-Language-Action models directly generate actions from multimodal observations, while World Action Models jointly model actions and future observations [ 2 , 29 ] .
Agentic policies provide another approach by selecting and invoking robot tools through repeated observation and reasoning [ 15 ] .
However, strong performance under standard evaluation conditions does not establish robustness to changes in visual evidence. Controlled perturbation benchmarks have demonstrated substantial performance degradation under variations in viewpoints, lighting, backgrounds, and other conditions [ 7 ] .
Reflections are not covered by these perturbations: rather than altering appearance, they duplicate task-relevant content at locations with a known geometric relationship to the physical scene.
blocks.zh:
通用机器人政策的最新进展扩大了从视觉和语言投入中可以完成的操纵任务的范围,然而这些政策是否具备上述两种能力仍不清楚。
远景-语言-行动模型直接产生来自多式联运观测的行动,而世界行动模型则联合了示范行动和未来观测[2,29].
代理政策通过反复观察和推理选择和引用机器人工具提供了另一种方法[15].
然而,在标准评价条件下的强效业绩并不能确定视觉证据的变化是否有力。 受控扰动基准显示,在观点、照明、背景和其他条件不同的情况下,性能大幅退化[7]。
这些扰动不涵盖反射:它们不是改变外观,而是在与物理场景有已知几何关系的地点重复与任务相关的内容.

blocks.en: Existing mirror-based evaluations have begun to examine embodied agents’ self-centric perception and interaction, including tasks inspired by mirror self-recognition [ 12 ] . We investigate a different operational setting: generalist policies performing external-object manipulation under controlled mirror configurations. The question posed above breaks down into three parts: how reflections affect task completion, whether observed degradation extends beyond the effects of an inserted physical panel, and what execution behaviors accompany these changes.
blocks.zh: 现有的以镜像为基础的评价已开始审查体现的代理人自我中心的认识和互动,包括由镜像自我承认所激发的任务[12]。 我们调查了不同的操作环境:在受控制的镜像配置下执行外物体操纵的通论政策. 以上提出的问题分为三个部分:反思如何影响任务的完成,观察到的退化是否超出插入的物理面板的效果,以及这些变化伴随什么执行行为.

blocks.en:
We introduce RoboDojo-Mirror, an evaluation benchmark built on RoboDojo [ 3 ] .
As illustrated in Fig. , it preserves the original manipulation objectives and success criteria while evaluating policies under four conditions: no mirror, a single mirror, dual mirrors, and a mirrored tabletop.
On a shared set of eight tasks, we pair layouts and policy seeds across conditions to measure changes relative to each policy’s own mirror-free baseline.
For selected policies, geometrically matched non-reflective panels provide additional controls for the effects of inserting physical structures.
We further design three diagnostic scenarios, namely grasping on a mirrored tabletop, pushing an object connected to its reflection, and acting with reflections as the main visual cue, combining task outcomes with trajectory and contact observations.
This protocol enables researchers to assess reflection
robustness using existing policies and task evaluators,
and to characterize failures beyond aggregate success rates.

blocks.en: 2.1 Robotic Manipulation Benchmarks and Visual Robustness
blocks.zh: 2.1 机器人操纵基准和视力

blocks.en:
Robotic manipulation benchmarks provide complementary tools for
evaluating policy capabilities.
LIBERO studies knowledge transfer in lifelong robot
learning [ 20 ] .
RoboTwin 2.0 combines scalable data generation with structured
domain randomization for bimanual
manipulation [ 4 ] , while RoboDojo provides
a unified simulation and real-world evaluation framework for
generalist manipulation policies [ 3 ] .
Recent benchmarks place greater emphasis on robustness beyond
nominal task success.
LIBERO-Plus introduces controlled perturbations to object layouts,
camera viewpoints, robot initial states, language, lighting,
backgrounds, and sensor observations [ 7 ] .
LIBERO-VPro evaluates closed-loop visual robustness by perturbing
the evidence available during execution, including observation
degradation, camera staleness, and cross-view
consistency [ 17 ] .

environmental, observational, execution, robot-state, and language
dimensions [ 35 ] .

metrics under clutter and controlled
perturbations [ 18 ] .
Building on these evaluation principles, our work focuses on
mirror-augmented manipulation, where reflections introduce
structured visual ambiguity alongside physical scene changes.
We evaluate task outcomes and contact behavior, and use
geometrically matched non-reflective panels to examine
performance differences beyond the presence of the panel itself.

blocks.en: 2.2 Mirror Perception and Spatial Reasoning
blocks.zh: 2.2 镜像感知和空间理性

blocks.en:
Mirrors challenge visual understanding because reflected objects
can resemble directly observed objects while occupying different
physical locations.
Early mirror-detection methods identify reflective regions through
contextual contrasts [ 28 ] , while video-based
approaches exploit spatial and temporal
correspondences [ 19 ] .
These methods address the localization of mirror regions rather
than the action consequences of reflected observations.
Mirror3D further estimates mirror geometry to refine unreliable depth measurements on reflective surfaces [ 26 ] .
More recently, MIRA-Bench evaluates reflection-aware perception,
spatial reasoning, and scene-level decisions in real RGB-D mirror
scenes, exposing difficulties in reconciling reflected appearance
with depth measurements [ 30 ] .
MirrorQA examines subject-centered left–right reasoning in
mirror contexts [ 21 ] .
Related diagnostic benchmarks, including
HallusionBench [ 11 ] and
IllusionVQA [ 25 ] , investigate visual
illusions and failures of image-grounded reasoning.
Unlike these perception-focused studies, we evaluate task outcomes and contact behavior during closed-loop manipulation under reflections.

blocks.en: 2.3 Mirror-Mediated Robotic Interaction
blocks.zh: 2.3 模拟机器人互动

blocks.en:
Robotic mirror research spans geometry and sensorimotor learning.
Hart and Scassellati infer mirror viewpoints from learned sensorimotor relationships [ 14 ] .
Marchand and Chaumette develop visual servoing for robot-mounted mirrors [ 22 ] , while Lanillos et al. combine active inference and sensorimotor prediction for mirror self-recognition and self/other distinction [ 16 ] .
Yoshioka et al. exploit mirror reflections to observe
occluded regions, while UMI incorporates side mirrors
for manipulation and shows that corrected mirror views
can outperform uncorrected ones [ 31 , 6 ] .
Recent embodied evaluations extend mirror-based tests to
multimodal agents.
MirrorBench studies self-centric intelligence through simulated
mirror interaction [ 12 ] , while
Ziliotto et al. evaluate whether agents can infer hidden
self-attributes from reflections and use this evidence to guide
actions [ 36 ] .
Beyond self-centric tasks, Being-M0.7 evaluates mirror-assisted
grasping of a directly occluded toy in a real-world humanoid
task [ 33 ] .
Our work studies reflection robustness across multiple
generalist policies and manipulation tasks under controlled
mirror configurations.

blocks.en: 3 Benchmark Design and Evaluation Protocol
blocks.zh: 3 基准设计和评价议定书

blocks.en: Built on RoboDojo [ 3 ] , RoboDojo-Mirror evaluates policy robustness to reflections while preserving the original task objectives and success criteria. Fig. 2 summarizes the paired evaluation protocol and controls.
blocks.zh: 建在RoboDojo上 [3],RoboDojo-Mirror评价政策稳健性进行反思,同时保留最初的任务目标和成功标准. 图2概述了配对的评价协议和控制。

blocks.en: 3.1 Policy and Task Selection
blocks.zh: 3.1 政策和任务选择

blocks.en: We evaluate five policies spanning Vision-Language-Action models, World Action Models, and agentic policies: WALL-OSS-1.0-Lite (WALL-OSS) [ 27 ] , VPP2 [ 13 ] , Awomo-0.5 [ 1 ] , Rex-M1 Preview [ 9 ] , and GPT-6-Astra (Astra) [ 34 , 23 ] . This selection covers different approaches to generating robot actions from visual observations.
blocks.zh: 我们评价了五项政策,涉及愿景-语言-行动模式、世界行动模式和代理政策: WALL-OSS-1.0-Lite(WALL-OSS) [27],VPP2 [13],Awomo-0.5 [1],Rex-M1预览 [9],以及GPT-6-Astra (Astra) [34,23]. 这一选择涵盖了从视觉观测中生成机器人动作的不同方法.

blocks.en:
For open-weight policies, we use official checkpoints and inference configurations.
Within each policy, we hold the checkpoint, observation interface, action interface, and inference settings fixed across scene conditions.
For Astra, the available camera streams, robot-state interface, motion tools, and inference budget are likewise held fixed across conditions.
blocks.zh:
对于开放重量政策,我们使用官方检查站和推断配置。
在每项政策中,我们把检查站、观察界面、行动界面和推断设置固定在现场条件之间。
对于Astra来说,现有的相机流,机器人状态接口,运动工具和推论预算同样被固定在各种条件之间.

blocks.en:
We select a shared eight-task set 𝒯 \mathcal{T} that balances diverse manipulation requirements with strong overall RoboDojo leaderboard performance.
All policies are evaluated on 𝒯 \mathcal{T} under four conditions, using paired comparisons against their own mirror-free baselines. The tasks are listed in the supplementary material.

我们选择一个共享的八任务集 T\ mathcal{T} 来平衡不同的操纵要求和强大的 RoboDojo 领导板的整体性能 。
所有政策在四个条件下在 T\ mathcal{T} 上评价, 用对比比较来对比它们自己的无镜基线 。 有关任务在补充材料中列出。

blocks.en: 3.2 Mirror Configurations
blocks.zh: 3.2 镜像配置

blocks.en: We construct four scene conditions from each task layout: no mirror, a single vertical mirror, dual vertical mirrors, and a mirrored tabletop. These conditions vary the placement and geometry of reflections while retaining matched initial object and robot states.
blocks.zh: 我们从每个任务布局中构建四个场景条件:没有镜像,一个单一的垂直镜像,两个垂直镜像,以及一个镜像的台顶. 这些条件在保留匹配的初始物体和机器人状态的同时,会改变反射的布置和几何.

blocks.en: Figure 2 : Overview of the evaluation protocol in RoboDojo-Mirror. Policies are evaluated on matched task layouts under four scene conditions, with additional non-reflective panel controls for selected policies.
blocks.zh: 图2:RoboDojo-Mirror的评价协议概览. 在四个场景条件下,对相应的任务布局进行政策评价,并对选定的政策进行额外的非反射面板控制。

blocks.en: No Mirror. We retain the original RoboDojo scene as the baseline.
blocks.zh: 无明镜. 我们保留原有的RoboDojo场景作为基线.

blocks.en: Single Mirror. A vertical planar mirror is placed near a tabletop edge, with its plane parallel to that edge and its reflective side facing the manipulation area.
blocks.zh: 单镜. 垂直平面镜被放置在平面边缘附近,它的平面与该边缘平行,反射面面对操纵区.

blocks.en: Dual Mirrors. Two vertical mirrors are placed along adjacent sides of the workspace, with mutually perpendicular planes and reflective faces oriented toward the manipulation area. This configuration introduces reflections from both mirrors and may also show higher-order reflections, depending on visibility and rendering settings.
blocks.zh: 双镜. 沿着工作空间的相邻侧面放置了两面垂直镜,两面是相互垂直的平面和面向操纵区的反射面. 这种配置引入了两面镜的反射,也可能根据能见度和渲染设置显示更高顺序的反射.

blocks.en: Mirrored Tabletop. We replace the tabletop’s surface material with a reflective finish while retaining its position and dimensions. Reflections therefore appear near the objects and the surface on which manipulation takes place.
blocks.zh: 明镜台顶. 我们用反射完成的表层材料取代表层材料,同时保留其位置和尺寸。 因此,在进行操纵的物体和表面附近出现了反射。

blocks.en: For the single-mirror and dual-mirror conditions, we shift the panels by 5 cm away from the robot relative to their initial construction positions, providing additional clearance while retaining visible reflections. The panels are fixed in the scene. This placement does not guarantee collision-free execution; contact with the panels is therefore recorded separately from task success.

blocks.en: Contact and behavior logging. We record visual observations, robot states, and action trajectories throughout each rollout. For episodes with valid contact measurements, we additionally monitor physical interactions with the mirror panel. We define the contact episode rate as the proportion of episodes involving at least one recorded contact with the panel.

blocks.en: 4 Performance under Mirror Conditions
blocks.zh: 4 镜像条件下的表现

blocks.en:
Following Section 3 , we report overall performance, mirror–panel comparisons, targeted behavioral diagnostics, and real-world validation.
Trajectory, video, and contact analyses characterize three observed behaviors: collision, phantom targeting, and spatial mislocalization.
blocks.zh:
第3节之后,我们将报告总体业绩、镜像-小板对比、有针对性的行为诊断和现实世界验证。
轨迹、视频和接触分析是三种观察到行为的特点:碰撞、幽灵瞄准和空间错位。

blocks.en: Collision. The robot contacts the mirror during execution, potentially disrupting manipulation. We distinguish such contact events from task failures, as contact does not necessarily cause failure.
blocks.zh: 碰撞 机器人在执行过程中接触镜像,可能干扰操纵. 我们将这些接触事件与任务失败区分开来,因为接触不一定会导致失败.

blocks.en: Phantom targeting. The robot directs manipulation actions toward a reflected object rather than its physical counterpart, suggesting that the reflection is treated as an actionable target.
blocks.zh: 幽灵瞄准 机器人将操纵动作指向一个反射的物体,而不是其物理对应物,暗示反射被视作可操作的目标.

blocks.en: Spatial mislocalization. The robot acts at an incorrect location relative to the physical target, resulting in missed grasps or ineffective manipulation without clear evidence of phantom targeting.
blocks.zh: 空间错位. 机器人相对于物理目标在不正确的位置上行动,导致在没有明确的奇幻目标证据的情况下,错失了抓住或无效的操纵.

blocks.en: 4.1 Overall Performance
blocks.zh: 4.1 总体业绩

blocks.en: Table 1 reports task scores and success rates aggregated over the task set, with each policy compared against its own mirror-free baseline.
blocks.zh: 表1报告任务分数和成功率与任务组合的汇总情况,每项政策与自己的无镜基线进行比较。

blocks.en:
All five policies achieve mirror-free success rates of 60.8–72.5%, and every mirror configuration reduces their aggregate success rates.
The average paired SR drops range from 10.8 to 56.7 percentage points across policies.
With a mirrored tabletop, VPP2 drops from 72.5% to 27.5%, while Rex-M1 Preview drops from 66.7% to 4.2%. Task scores also decrease under all mirror configurations.
blocks.zh:
所有五个政策都实现了60.8-72.5%的无镜成功率,每个镜像配置都会降低其总的成功率.
平均对等的SR下降幅度从10.8%到56.7个百分点不等。
使用镜像台式机,VPP2从72.5%下降到27.5%,而Rex-M1预览从66.7%下降到4.2%。 在所有镜像配置下任务分数也会减少.

blocks.en: Overall, dual mirrors tend to cause greater performance degradation than single mirrors, with VPP2 as an exception. WALL-OSS and Awomo-0.5 reach their lowest success rates under dual mirrors, whereas VPP2, Rex-M1 Preview, and Astra perform worst with a mirrored tabletop.
blocks.zh: 总体而言,双镜往往比单镜造成更大的性能退化,VPP2是例外. WALL-OSS和Awomo-0.5在双镜下达到最低成功率,而VPP2,Rex-M1预览,以及Astra在镜像台上表现最差.

blocks.en: Astra shows little aggregate change under a single mirror (65.0% to 62.5%), but its SR decreases to 52.5% under dual mirrors and 47.5% with a mirrored tabletop. Despite the highest recorded robot–mirror contact rates under single and dual mirrors (55.0% and 85.0%), Astra exhibits relatively small SR drops, suggesting that contact occurrence alone does not explain performance degradation.
blocks.zh: Astra在单镜下显示总体变化不大(65.0%到62.5%),但其SR在双镜下下降至52.5%,在镜面台上则下降至47.5%。 尽管在单镜和双镜下录制的机器人-镜像接触率最高(55.0%和85.0%),但Astra显示的SR降幅相对较小,说明仅接触发生并不能解释性能退化的原因.

blocks.en:
Since execution budgets differ across policies, these aggregates should not be interpreted as a controlled cross-policy ranking.
Furthermore, task outcomes alone cannot separate visual interference from physical obstruction, motivating the mirror–panel comparisons in the next subsection.
blocks.zh:
由于各政策的执行预算不同,因此不应将这些总额解释为控制性交叉政策排名。
此外,单凭任务结果无法将视觉干扰与物理障碍区分开来,从而刺激下一节的镜像-小板比较。

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
We introduce RoboDojo-Mirror to evaluate robotic
manipulation under controlled mirror configurations.
Paired evaluations across five policies and real-world
experiments show lower success rates under mirrors.
Matched panel controls show that direct collisions alone cannot explain the performance degradation. Behavioral diagnostics reveal patterns consistent with phantom targeting and spatial mislocalization.
These findings expose difficulties in connecting
visual observations to effective physical actions
and establish reflection robustness as a concrete
target for evaluating and improving robot policies.

匹配的面板控制显示,仅靠直接碰撞无法解释性能退化. 行为诊断揭示出与幽灵瞄准和空间错位一致的模式.
这些结论暴露了在将残疾人与残疾人联系起来方面的困难。
对有效物理动作的视觉观察
并确立反射坚固度,作为具体
评估和改进机器人政策的目标。
